scope.objective: Prove that the full-source package graph is complete and privacy-safe, then exercise a disposable local install from v1.2.17, upgrade to the exact current full-source package, and rollback to v1.2.17 without mutating operator credential, trust, or session state.

productionTree.canonicalization: UTF-8 sorted production paths from the FS0 constitution; JSON array of {path,mode,size,sha256}; aggregate SHA-256 is domain plus canonical JSON bytes

preArtifactWorkingTreeObservation.disposition: Dirty user-owned development tree retained. Exact production identity is local implementation evidence only; no clean or frozen release candidate is claimed.

packageGraphContract.fullSource: The current package dry-run contains every production module reachable from the shipped Piagent guard and CLI entrypoints, including packages/piagent-core/runtime/recovery/resume-state.ts.
packageGraphContract.rcReadinessBinding: The install-migration-rollback RC test group now explicitly includes tests/package-install-rollback.test.mjs, so later readiness evaluation cannot pass this group using only the older fixture set.

lifecycleContract.baseline: A source archive is built from the immutable historical tag v1.2.17^{} and packed as the exact rollback artifact.
lifecycleContract.candidate: The exact current working source is copied to a disposable directory, assigned synthetic version 1.3.0-fs2.4 only inside that directory, and packed locally. The synthetic version is test identity, not a release-candidate identity.
lifecycleContract.install: npm install --global --ignore-scripts targets an isolated temporary prefix and cache; the installed baseline reports 1.2.17 and does not contain the current-only resume-state module.
lifecycleContract.upgrade: Installing the disposable current-source tarball into the same prefix reports 1.3.0-fs2.4, contains the current-only module with the exact working-source SHA-256, and exposes a working piagent-doctor help command.
lifecycleContract.rollback: Reinstalling the v1.2.17 tarball reports 1.2.17, removes the current-only module, and exposes a working piagent-install help command.
lifecycleContract.cleanup: All archives, package roots, npm prefixes, caches, and synthetic operator homes are created below disposable temporary roots and removed after each test.

privacyAndStateContract.operatorFixture: A private temporary Pi operator tree contains synthetic auth, settings, trust, and session files with 0700 directories and 0600 files.
privacyAndStateContract.proof: A domain-separated recursive identity over type, path, POSIX mode, and file bytes is identical before install, after upgrade, and after rollback.

declaredCiFixture.coverage: The package-install-rollback regression is part of tests/*.test.mjs and therefore runs on both declared workflow runners.

platformEvidence.boundary: This artifact proves the macOS execution and the deterministic Linux CI/fixture wiring. It does not claim that an external Linux runner or exact RC artifact has executed.

verification.command: node --test tests/install-global.test.mjs tests/update-global.test.mjs tests/global-update.test.mjs tests/migrate-project-state.test.mjs tests/uninstall-global.test.mjs tests/package-distribution.test.mjs tests/release-identity.test.mjs tests/package-install-rollback.test.mjs
piagent-capabilities doctor with repository profile and lock

authorityAndMigration.releaseIdentityChange: none; the synthetic candidate version exists only inside the disposable test package root
authorityAndMigration.stateCompatibility: The test exercises the existing v1.2.17 install/update/rollback boundary without modifying user or project state.

rollback.mechanism: Remove the additive package lifecycle regression and remove it from the RC install-migration-rollback test group.

limitations: This is exact-current local implementation evidence on a dirty development tree, not a clean or frozen release candidate.
The current-source tarball uses a synthetic disposable version solely to prove upgrade/rollback mechanics; it is not a v1.3.0 RC artifact.
The package lifecycle executed locally on macOS ARM64. Ubuntu and macOS workflow wiring is verified from the current CI fixture, but no external Linux execution is claimed.
No provider, benchmark, registry write, user/system global install, branch, worktree, commit, tag, push, publish, candidate freeze, cleanup of user files, or CF-FS2-05 gate work was performed.
